title: A Bernoulli-restricted CNF collapses to a narrow DNF
statement:
Let $g$ be a CNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and suppose that within each clause no two distinct literals share a variable and no literal is repeated. Fix a natural number $l$ and a real parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, so in particular $p \le 1$. Then, drawing a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability that the restricted function $g|_\rho$ (the function $x \mapsto g(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ on the free coordinates) cannot be computed exactly by any DNF formula of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]

replaced:
The dual statement. Let $g$ be a $\mathrm{CNF}$ of width at most $w>0$ (with distinct
variables per clause and no duplicate literals), let $n>0$, and let $0<p\le \tfrac{1}{40w}$
with $p\le 1$. Then the probability under a Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction $\rho$ that $g|_\rho$
cannot be expressed as a $\mathrm{DNF}$ of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^l + \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{np}{3}\Bigr).
\]
